jobs.title: Sales Internship - Beauty at Volaant
jobs.description: Employer: Volaant Expires: 08/11/2026 Sales & Marketing Internship Volaant — Clinical Luxury SkincareLocation: RemoteDuration: Full-time summer internship, June 12 – September 12, 2026Compensation: CommissionReports to: Founder & CEOPath forward: Strong performers will be offered a paid part-time or full-time role after the internship concludes About VolaantVolaant is a clinical luxury skincare brand built on pharmaceutical-grade formulation and refined aesthetic. Our products serve the most discerning consumers and the most exacting professional channels — board-certified dermatologists, plastic surgeons, and medical aesthetic spas across the country.We launch summer 2026 with a founder-led sales strategy that puts our products directly into the hands of leading clinical practices. This internship gives you a seat at the table for that launch. About the OpportunityThis is a real sales role with real responsibility. You will be trained directly by our Founder & CEO — a seasoned, exited serial entrepreneur with two decades of experience scaling companies from launch through exit, including hands-on sales leadership at the CRO and CEO level.You will learn how to sell into one of the most sophisticated buyer audiences in the country: highly educated physician-owners and medical professionals who demand clinical credibility, ingredient transparency, and substance over hype. The skills you build here translate directly into careers in medical device sales, pharmaceutical sales, biotech, healthcare technology, luxury goods, or any field where you need to sell credibly to educated, high-value buyers.If you’ve ever wondered what real B2B sales looks like at a luxury brand — the prospecting, the pitch development, the in-person demos, the follow-ups, the close — this is where you’ll learn it. Not from a textbook. From doing it. Why This Role Is ExcitingYou’ll get to immerse yourself in everything beauty, skincare, and clinical formulation. You’ll talk about active ingredients, formulation chemistry, brand positioning, and the science behind why our products work. You’ll meet practitioners doing some of the most interesting work in aesthetic medicine. You’ll walk into med spas, dermatology clinics, and plastic surgery practices and represent a brand you genuinely believe in.If you love skincare and beauty, this is a dream role. You’re not selling something you have to justify — you’re selling a clinical luxury product you’d want yourself.And you’ll do it alongside a founder who has done this before, who will teach you the playbook in real time, and who will invest in your growth because your success is the brand’s success. What You’ll DoSales Pipeline Development• Research and identify target accounts: med spas, dermatology practices, plastic surgery offices, and aesthetic clinics in the Portland metro and beyond• Build and maintain the CRM pipeline in HubSpot• Schedule in-person demos and follow-up appointments• Prepare account-specific outreach materials and pitch decksIn-Person Demos and Founder Shadowing• Accompany the Founder & CEO on in-person sales demos to clinical accounts• Observe and gradually participate in founder-led sales conversations• Take detailed notes on objections, questions, and conversion patterns• Build the muscle memory of clinical B2B sales by watching it executed liveCustomer and Partner Communication TrainingYou will be trained to speak credibly with the most sophisticated buyers in beauty — board-certified dermatologists, plastic surgeons, NPs, and aesthetic medical spa owners. This is a skill that takes most early-career salespeople years to develop. You’ll get hands-on training from someone who has sold to executives, physicians, and sovereign clients across multiple industries.Pilot Program and Account Management• Support the paid clinical pilot program — onboarding new pilot accounts, tracking 30-day milestones, scheduling follow-up calls• Maintain account communications and ensure no opportunity falls through the cracks• Help convert pilot accounts into full wholesale relationships• Document case studies, testimonials, and clinical feedback from converted accountsStrategic Sales Projects• Contribute to corporate gifting outreach for the holiday season• Support sales materials development including the clinical leave-behind, pitch deck refinements, and email templates• Research and identify multi-location group opportunities (med spa groups with 5+ locations)• Help shape the sales playbook in real time as the brand scales What We’re Looking For• Entrepreneurial spirit — you take initiative, you’re comfortable in unstructured environments, and you move fast• Genuine skincare and beauty enthusiast — you actually care about the industry, the science, and the brands shaping it• Strong interpersonal skills — comfortable in professional settings, confident in conversation, able to read a room• Excellent verbal and written communication — clear, articulate, and credible when speaking with highly educated buyers• Coachability — you want to learn, you welcome feedback, and you apply it quickly• Resilience and self-direction — you don’t need to be micromanaged, and you handle a “no” without losing momentum• Working knowledge of AI tools — Claude, ChatGPT, or similar; you use them to research accounts, draft outreach, and work efficiently• Currently enrolled in college with the ability to receive academic credit for the internship• Reliable transportation preferred for in-person Portland metro field work, though not strictly required Who This Is Perfect ForThis internship is an exceptional fit if you’re studying or interested in:• Sales, marketing, or business development• Medical device or pharmaceutical sales (this role builds the foundation)• Healthcare, biotech, or life sciences• Skincare, beauty, or aesthetic medicine• Pre-med, pre-PA, or pre-nursing (with interest in commercial healthcare)• Entrepreneurship, brand-building, or luxury goodsYou do not need prior sales experience. You need curiosity, drive, professionalism, and a real interest in the industry. The skills will be taught. What You’ll Walk Away With• Hands-on training in real B2B clinical sales from an experienced CRO/CEO• The ability to speak credibly with physician-owners, dermatologists, and aesthetic medical professionals — a skill set that translates directly into medical device and pharmaceutical sales careers• A portfolio of closed accounts, pipeline development, and sales materials you contributed to• A direct mentorship relationship with a seasoned exited entrepreneur• Real-world sales process experience: prospecting, pitching, demoing, objection-handling, closing, account management• Professional references from a real launch• A first-look offer for a paid part-time or full-time role at Volaant after September 20 How to ApplySend the following to hello@volaant.com with the subject line “Sales Consultant Application – [Your Name]”:1. A brief introduction (3–5 sentences) on why this role is right for you and why you’re passionate about beauty2. Resume or LinkedIn profile3. One example of a time you communicated, persuaded, or led someone to a decision - could be from school, a campus role, a previous job, a side project, fundraising, or anything that demonstrates your ability to influence and follow through4. 3-5 minute video on why you want to work with us, and your favorite skincare or beauty brand and why5. Your city and confirmation that you have reliable transportationApplications reviewed on a rolling basis. Start date is immediate - we are hiring through mid June and onboarding new consultants weekly. 30 total roles which will remain open until filled.

jobs.title: Social Media Manager at SkyAccess
jobs.description: Employer: SkyAccess Expires: 08/12/2026 Private jets are the most cinematic content on earth, and we're 370,000 followers into proving it works on Instagram alone, over 500,000 across every platform we touch. Now we need someone to make it go viral again, and again, and again. You'll own the SkyAccess Instagram feed like a viral engineer: analyze what's landing on competitor accounts, generate carousels with Plot and every other tool you can point at content, put them out, measure what worked, iterate on the small details, and keep pushing the count. Long term you'll build the self-operating content system that runs the whole brand voice. Cracked, obsessed with taste, portfolio ready. We want someone who eats, breathes, and lives on Claude, using it as the second brain on every post you ship. Aviation is one of the last legendary industries left. Help us own the timeline. About SkyAccess: We're a private aviation marketplace based in Laguna Beach and West Los Angeles. Operators post empty-leg flights and travelers book them at a fraction of charter prices. We've gone from 0 to 1 (370,000 Instagram followers, over 500,000 across all platforms) and we're scaling the team for our next phase of growth. Location: Fully remote, anywhere in the United States. Compensation: Paid at $17.28 per hour (Los Angeles minimum wage), 30 hours per week. Ongoing role with room to grow into a leadership position running the entire content system. Open to current seniors, recent grads, and people who want to build a career in social. How to apply: Email your application to m@skyaccess.com with four required materials: (1) a resume, (2) a 1 to 3 minute video on why you want to work here and what value you would bring, (3) your best social content or accounts you have grown, and (4) something you have built with Claude or another AI tool. It doesn't have to be aviation-related, we just want to see how you think.

jobs.description: Employer: Stride Soles Expires: 08/15/2026 If you are interested in the role, please send an email to hiring@stridesoles.com with the subject line 'Marketing Intern'. About Stride SolesWe make custom orthotics the way they should be made: German podiatric engineering, manufactured in the USA, priced at a fraction of a clinic visit. Customers take a quiz, scan their feet with our iOS app, and get a prescription-grade orthotic designed for them. Think Warby Parker, but for the thing holding up your entire body.We are small, fast, and building something people actually feel under their feet every day. You will work directly with the founder and a tight team of operators, clinicians, and designers.The RoleWe are looking for a marketing intern who lives on Reddit and understands how real communities work. You know the difference between adding value and shilling.A track record you can show us. In your application, walk us through community or Reddit marketing you have actually done: campaigns you ran, communities you grew, posts that landed, and the results. Contact acciprecruiting@conservationlegacy.org Please submit a resume and cover letter via our website, www.appalachiancc.org/individualplacements. Applications will be accepted until August 1st. Appalachian Conservation Corps: Our Individual Placement program works to connect young people to conservation service work across Appalachia and neighboring communities in Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, DC, Ohio, and Pennsylvania. ACC is a program of Conservation Legacy, a nationwide network of conservation organizations. As an AmeriCorps program, participants commit to a term of service at their placement site in order to gain hands-on experience and a variety of benefits to help them succeed in achieving their career goals. ACC welcomes national applicants, but also emphasizes the engagement of local individuals who represent the communities in which they serve. National Park Service Chesapeake Gateways:Chesapeake Bay Gateways and Watertrails (NPS Chesapeake Gateways) is a partnership park statutorily directed by the Chesapeake Bay Initiative Act of 1998 to create, support, and invest in the Chesapeake Gateways Network. The Network is a system of over 300 public and private sector places, experiences, and communities in six states and Washington, D.C. within the Chesapeake Bay watershed. NPS Chesapeake Gateways invests in the Network through National Recreation & Preservation funding and full-time National Park Service expertise, as directed by Congress. Headquartered in Annapolis, MD, NPS Chesapeake Gateways has five core functions to convene, promote, support, and invest in the Network. The Chesapeake Gateways Network Framework guides the NPS, grounding the Network’s operations in its core functions as directed by Congress. Position Summary: Appalachian Conservation Corps and the National Park Service are seeking a Chesapeake Gateways Ambassador to work with National Park Service staff on projects to specifically support promotion of visitor experiences throughout the Chesapeake Gateways Network through digital and print resources. The member will review, develop, and implement processes to facilitate partnership communications and training and assist in the overall efforts to assist Chesapeake Gateways Places and Experiences in engaging visitors to the Chesapeake watershed.The member will complete two weeks of formal training at the NPS Chesapeake Gateways office to learn basic operations, skills in interpretation, and the natural/cultural resource stories that guide our collective work. Following this onboarding, the member will complete training specifically to supporting Places and Experiences network designations. Throughout the year, the member will work with partners to facilitate designations and support the partners in activating Network benefits. The member will assist other staff with planning and hosting at least eight community programs and the park’s annual network meeting. As part of this work, the member may work with the public and act as the face of NPS Chesapeake Gateways at public events, partner meetings, and while roving Chesapeake Gateways places or in the community. Responsibilities include but are not limited to:Support developing digital listings to highlight elements of Chesapeake Gateways with specific partners in alignment with Network general agreements.Contributes to the implementation of a professional digital presence based on strategic priorities for providing information to the public and partner organizations. Opportunities to participate in a variety of activities and projects related to the mission of the National Park Service depending on interest areas.Community engagement and outreach, especially regarding engagement and involvement of young people in cultural heritage. Participate in developing interpretation, programming, and experiences at Chesapeake Gateways Places and Experiences for watershed visitors.Link culture and nature through interpretation, education, messaging, and initiatives. Housing is not provided. Time Requirements:This position is full-time, 40 hours/week.This position is expected to serve Monday to Friday, with occasional weekend work. A half hour lunch break will not be counted towards AmeriCorps service.Member will have most federal holidays off but may be expected to work holidays during the busy summer season.Member may be required to participate in national, state, or local service projects or events as part of their service term. Benefits: $760 week stipend paid bi-weekly ($600 living stipend + $160 additional member benefit)$7,395 AmeriCorps Segal Education Award upon successful completion of 1700 hour service term (award amount varies based on length of commitment and can be used for paying off federal student loans or paying tuition for a Title IV accredited college) Option to enroll in free Health, Vision, Mental Health and Dental benefits$1250 professional development fund for certifications, trainings, conferences, and travel reimbursementsPaid leaveEligibility for the Public Land Corps Hiring Authority upon successful completion – noncompetitive hiring status for two years when applying for federal positions.Possible federal student loan forbearance and interest payoffMember Assistance Program – 3 free sessions of support with a counseling or work-life balance specialist Depending upon the academic institution and program, positions may fulfill Individual Internship requirements Professional development opportunities (mentorship, resume support, alumni listserv, etc.) and exposure to natural resource career paths Preferred Qualifications:Some college course work completed in Communications, History, Public Affairs, Public Speaking, or other related subjectsExperience working in public facing roles and customer service Minimum Requirements: To qualify for this AmeriCorps position, you must be between the ages of 21 and 30, and a US citizen that has received a high school diploma or GED. Contact ACCrecruiting@conservationlegacy.org Please submit a resume and cover letter via our website, www.appalachiancc.org/individualplacements. Applications will be accepted until August 1st. Appalachian Conservation Corps: Our Individual Placement program works to connect young people to conservation service work across Appalachia and neighboring communities in Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, DC, Ohio, and Pennsylvania. ACC is a program of Conservation Legacy, a nationwide network of conservation organizations. As an AmeriCorps program, participants commit to a term of service at their placement site in order to gain hands-on experience and a variety of benefits to help them succeed in achieving their career goals. ACC welcomes national applicants, but also emphasizes the engagement of local individuals who represent the communities in which they serve. National Park Service Chesapeake Gateways:Chesapeake Bay Gateways and Watertrails (NPS Chesapeake Gateways) is a partnership park statutorily directed by the Chesapeake Bay Initiative Act of 1998 to create, support, and invest in the Chesapeake Gateways Network. The Network is a system of over 300 public and private sector places, experiences, and communities in six states and Washington, D.C. within the Chesapeake Bay watershed. NPS Chesapeake Gateways invests in the Network through National Recreation & Preservation funding and full-time National Park Service expertise, as directed by Congress. Headquartered in Annapolis, MD, NPS Chesapeake Gateways has five core functions to convene, promote, support, and invest in the Network. The Chesapeake Gateways Network Framework guides the NPS, grounding the Network’s operations in its core functions as directed by Congress. Position Summary: Appalachian Conservation Corps and the National Park Service are seeking a Chesapeake Gateways Ambassador to work with National Park Service staff to work on projects to specifically support promotion of visitor experiences throughout the Chesapeake Gateways Network through digital and print resources. The member will review, develop, and implement processes to facilitate partnership communications and training and assist in the overall efforts to assist Chesapeake Gateways Places and Experiences in engaging visitors to the Chesapeake watershed.The member will complete two weeks of formal training at the NPS Chesapeake Gateways office to learn basic operations, skills in interpretation, and the natural/cultural resource stories that guide our collective work. In addition to the standard training curriculum, the member will participate in self-paced digital media training specific to the National Park Service. The member will work with the park’s visitor experience team to research and write digital media content, highlighting Chesapeake Gateways Places and Experiences. They will also participate in a strategic development planning process to help guide the future of the park’s social media strategy. After working at Chesapeake Gateways for several months, the member will independently create or co-create content with partners for the park’s website. This content development will include written content, as well as audio visual elements. The member may assist with other interpretive media projects including signage, and brochures. Responsibilities include but are not limited to:Community engagement and outreach, especially activating young people to move from digital engagement to onsite stewardship. Preparing and publishing content focused on at least one of the NPS Chesapeake Gateways themes. Creating, editing, and publishing content for multiple print and digital platforms including websites, mobile apps, social media, publications, newspapers, magazines, and more. Developing digital interpretative experiences at Chesapeake Gateways Places.Develop common interpretive content that can be readily adapted and customized for use at individual sites, including thematic interpretive products, such as interpretive signage. Link culture and nature through interpretation, education, messaging, and initiatives. Opportunities to participate in a variety of activities and projects related to the mission of the National Park Service depending on interest areas. Housing is not provided. Time Requirements:These positions are full-time, 40 hours/week.This position is expected to serve Monday to Friday, with occasional weekend work. A half hour lunch break will not be counted towards AmeriCorps service.Member will have most federal holidays off but may be expected to work holidays during the busy summer season.Member may be required to participate in national, state, or local service projects or events as part of their service term. Benefits: $760 week stipend paid bi-weekly ($600 living stipend + $160 additional member benefit)$7,395 AmeriCorps Segal Education Award upon successful completion of 1700 hour service term (award amount varies based on length of commitment and can be used for paying off federal student loans or paying tuition for a Title IV accredited college) Option to enroll in free Health, Vision, Mental Health and Dental benefits$1250 professional development fund for certifications, trainings, conferences, and travel reimbursementsPaid leaveEligibility for the Public Land Corps Hiring Authority upon successful completion – noncompetitive hiring status for two years when applying for federal positions.Possible federal student loan forbearance and interest payoffMember Assistance Program – 3 free sessions of support with a counseling or work-life balance specialist Depending upon the academic institution and program, positions may fulfill Internship requirements Professional development opportunities (mentorship, resume support, alumni listserv, etc.) and exposure to natural resource career paths Preferred Qualifications:Some college course work completed in Communications, History, Public Affairs, Public Speaking, or other related subjectsExperience working in public facing roles and customer service Minimum Requirements: To qualify for this AmeriCorps position, you must be between the ages of 21 and 30, and a US citizen that has received a high school diploma or GED. All offers of employment are conditional upon completion of an acceptable check of the National Sex Offender Public Registry and federal criminal background check. Must be eligible to receive an AmeriCorps Education Award.Possess a valid driver’s license Evaluation and Reporting:As an AmeriCorps member, performance will be evaluated on whether the member has completed the required number of hours, the member has satisfactorily completed assignments, and if the member has met other performance criteria that were clearly communicated at the beginning of the term of service.Reporting requirements include, but are not limited to, bi-weekly timesheets and accomplishment tracking. jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Graphic Design Intern at The Autoimmune Fund
jobs.description: Employer: The Autoimmune Fund Expires: 08/20/2026 Information Design InternThe Autoimmune FundSummer 2026 start, continuing through fall and beyond | Part-Time, Paid | Los Angeles (In-Person, walking distance to UCLA)Do you think in color, type, and layout? Can you take a messy pile of ideas and turn it into something people actually want to look at? Do you get a little thrill when a slide finally clicks? Perfect. And if you are the kind of person who notices when a number on that slide looks off, even better. The Autoimmune Fund is looking for a Graphic Design Intern to help us give an overlooked category the visual identity it has never had.To applyEmail your resume and, most importantly, a portfolio (a link or PDF of slides, graphics, or visual work) to bonnie@autoimmune.fund, with the subject line [Your Name] Graphic Design Intern 2026. A short note on why you want to work with Dr. Bonnie Feldman, and what kind of design you love making, goes a long way.Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Strong candidates may be invited to a short, paid design exercise so we can see how you think, not just what you have already made. The exercise will include working with a small set of real numbers, so we can see how you handle data as well as layout. Do not wait to apply.You will only be considered if you email your documents. Please do not submit through Handshake alone.Why it mattersAutoimmune disease affects more than 50 million Americans, and roughly 80% of them are women. Most wait years for a diagnosis and a lifetime for better treatments. Capital never organized around this the way it did around cancer, and one big reason is that no one has made the problem visible. That is the work: using design to help investors, and the world, finally see the millions of patients behind the numbers. Every deck, chart, and graphic you make moves that forward.The Autoimmune Fund is the first venture fund dedicated exclusively to autoimmune and immune-mediated disease. We invest at the Seed and Series A stages across diagnostics, therapeutics, devices, digital health, and new care models in a $150B+ market that, until now, has had no visual language. That is where you come in.What you'll doThis role sits at the intersection of design, science, and storytelling, and no two weeks look exactly the same. You will:Design and polish investor pitch decks, portfolio updates, and presentation materials that are clean, on-brand, and genuinely compelling.Turn complex science and real data into clear, accurate charts, diagrams, and visual explainers. A lot of this role is making numbers legible, so getting the figures right matters as much as making them look good.Design visually stunning ebooks and long-form guides, from cover to interior pages.Create social and LinkedIn graphics, one-pagers, and newsletter visuals in the fund's voice.Help build and maintain templates, a color palette, and a consistent visual identity across everything we produce.Support the design of our flagship publication, The Immune Decade: 2026 Report, a first-of-its-kind institutional report on the autoimmune market.Experiment with AI design and productivity tools to work faster and try more ideas.Did we lose you at “investor” or “LPs”? Do not worry. We do not expect you to arrive knowing venture capital. If this world feels unfamiliar, that is exactly why you should apply. We will teach you the science and the strategy. You bring the eye, and a comfort with getting the numbers right.Who you'll work withYou will work closely with our founder and CEO, Dr. Bonnie Feldman (DDS, MBA), a former clinical dentist, Wall Street equity research analyst, and venture-backed startup founder. She has spoken at TEDx and Stanford Medicine X, she is equal parts strategist and storyteller, and she is always up for a good brainstorm. You will also collaborate with our founding fellows on the science and investment sides, so you will never be designing in a vacuum.What you'll getReal work, made for real audiences, with real stakes. You will walk away with polished decks, graphics, and framework visuals designed for institutional investors and healthcare leaders, plus a front-row seat to how a specialized venture fund gets built. And the work adds up to something bigger than a portfolio: the clearer we make this category, the more capital flows to the treatments and care patients have been waiting decades for.Hours & perksWe are looking for a part-time start in Summer 2026 that continues through the fall and beyond, ideally a full-year commitment spanning 2026 and 2027. This is a paid role (hourly or stipend), roughly 10 to 20 hours per week, with scheduling flexible around your classes. It is in-person, based in Dr. Feldman's home office within walking distance of the UCLA campus, so you will need to be in Los Angeles. Perks include meals prepared by a private chef and plenty of coffee.QualificationsA graduate student in design (preferred), a student on a gap year, or a 4th-year undergraduate at UCLA or an equivalent program.Based in Los Angeles and able to work in person near UCLA.A portfolio that shows a strong eye for layout, typography, color, and hierarchy, ideally including ebook or editorial layout, and a chart or data-driven graphic if you have one. We care more about clarity and taste than polish.Comfortable with numbers and data. You do not need to love statistics or have a math background, but you do need to read a chart, notice when a figure looks wrong, and represent data accurately. A chart that looks good and says the wrong thing does not help us.Fluent in a few design tools such as Figma, Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, Google Slides, or PowerPoint.Curious, quick to learn, open to feedback, and comfortable in a fast-paced environment.A bonus, not a requirement: interest in science or healthcare, or prior work in data visualization.Has a personality (yes, really).

jobs.description: Employer: Eve Inc. Expires: 08/20/2026 Ode Founding AmbassadorYou're already the person who makes plans happen. Come do it on purpose.Five students. One campus. You won't be handing out flyers for ode - you'll be deciding what Ode is at Georgia Tech.Every campus has a handful of people who are the reason anything happens. No scripts. No approved captions. If it sounds like marketing, we've failed you.Your monthYour first 100. A hundred people from your world, on ode because of you. Not cold outreach - your dorm, your major, your people. These become the first hundred humans on a campus that's about to feel very different.Coffee with the founder. Not a check-in. A conversation.Your semesterOne activation that's yours. Your idea, our budget, your name on it.What you get$100/week, plus $200 in incentives per semester. For making plans with your friends. We're aware of how that sounds.Founding merch at the kickoff dinner. A small number of people will ever have it. You'll be one of them.In the room, all summer and through launch week. Every founding-team dinner, every late night, every "should we actually do this" - you're there.A direct line to Aditi. Text, call, Slack, 1 a.m., whatever. Not a manager. A collaborator.A letter of recommendation that actually means something - from someone who watched you build a thing from zero, for internships, grad school, and full-time roles.First pick on ode roles as we grow. You were here first. That will always be true.Public "Founding Five" credit at launch - LinkedIn, press, Ode's own channels. Whatever Ode becomes, there will be five names attached to how it started.The detailsJuly 30 - November 30, with the option to keep going into spring. About 5–7 hours a week - roughly a dinner and a coffee.Who we're actually looking forConnectors. The person in the dorm, the major, the friend group who already makes plans happen. We care about action, not polish. If you read this and thought that's literally me - it probably is.Five spots. Tell us why it's you.

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Marketing Intern at Doc Wealth
jobs.description: Employer: Doc Wealth Expires: 08/27/2026 Marketing Intern (Year-Round, Path to Full-Time)We're building the largest physician-focused tax company in the country, growing faster than anyone in this space. This role sits inside the marketing team and touches everything: what we publish, what we spend, and whether the growth engine actually compounds. Read the whole post before applying.This is not make-a-mood-board-and-watch. You'll be publishing real content under our name, running real campaigns with real budgets behind them, and owning numbers that leadership actually looks at. Real deadlines, real consequences, with the Marketing Manager beside you and modern AI tooling at your back. The pace is fast and the standard is high. You'll learn more here in a few months than in a year anywhere else, because we hand you real responsibility and expect you to rise to it. Hard on purpose. If that sounds like too much, this is the wrong post.We need an absolute ninja. Someone who comes in, learns how the marketing engine actually works, and takes ownership of pieces of it with due time.You'll doContent and channelsWrite across everything we publish: blog posts, emails, landing pages, social content, campaign copy. What you write goes live.Support SEO research, format and optimize blog content, and build and maintain website pages.Schedule and publish across our social channels, then track what performs and say why.Engage physician conversations across forums, social platforms, and the communities where our audience already spends time. You'll be speaking as the firm, so precision matters.Build graphics and marketing assets to support campaigns across channels.Campaigns and operationsEmail: build and proof campaigns before they go out, manage list segmentation, and catch the typo before ten thousand physicians see it.Paid media: support campaign assets, pull performance data, and track results against goals.Partnerships: track deliverables across partner programs and keep co-branded content moving. Nobody chases you; you chase them.Events and webinars: promotional assets, registration pages, post-event follow-up.Analytics: keep tracking and attribution clean, build regular performance reports, and dig into what's working and what isn't. When a number looks wrong, find out why before someone asks.Research: track competitors and market trends, and surface what's worth acting on.Growth projects: help launch channels and platforms we don't have yet.Use AI and automation so your reps go to judgment, not busywork.Who this is forThe sharpest person in your program. Learns fast, works hard without being told twice, energized by a heavy workload. Three things we care about most:Writing. You write clean, tight copy that doesn't need a rewrite before it ships. You know the difference between words that fill space and words that move someone. Be ready to show a writing sample or write something on the spot.Detail. Marketing looks polished or sloppy based entirely on the small things: the broken link, the wrong UTM, the subject line that renders badly on mobile. You catch these before they go out, not after.Numbers and follow-through. You think in steps and notice when something doesn't add up. A campaign's attribution is off, a partner deliverable is nine days late, two reports disagree on last month's leads. You catch it and say something instead of moving on.And be honest with yourself about the manual work. A lot of this is scheduling, formatting, data cleanup, and tracking spreadsheets. It is not always interesting. It still has to be right, because everything downstream depends on it. If tedious-but-important work drains you, this is not the right seat.This is not for anyone who needs hand-holding or wants a comfortable lane.Boundary on scope: anything carrying real brand or spend exposure (budget decisions, public statements on tax positions, partner commitments) is yours to prepare and the Marketing Manager's to decide. You will never be left holding that alone.The path: Perform and you convert to full-time, then keep climbing. Earned, not given.Selection: We screen hard. Very few who apply are selected. If you're the right person, that should make you want this more.Details$14 to $20 an hour, 30 to 40 hours per week.Fully remote.Year-round, running through until you graduate.A flexible schedule built around your classes.RequirementsPursuing a degree in marketing or a related program.Strong written communication. Be ready to prove it.Organized, accurate, fast. Comfortable in spreadsheets and picking up new tools and platforms quickly.Familiar with marketing channels and how they connect to each other.Curious about a niche industry. Physician tax is more interesting than it sounds.Prior marketing experience is a plus: an internship, a class project, a club, or something you built yourself.Hungry to grow into a full-time role and own it.

jobs.title: Program Operations Analyst Intern at Keck Medicine of USC
jobs.description: Employer: Keck Medicine of USC Expires: 01/01/2027 Please DO NOT CONTACT members of the Keck Medicine of USC organization about this position. All inquiries regarding our postings must be made to itinterns@med.usc.edu or through one of the program's other mediums; LinkedIn (Keck Medicine of USC IS Intern Program) or Instagram (@KeckISIntern). ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------Information Services of Keck Medicine of USC is seeking students to join our team during a time of tremendous growth. We are looking for high-energy, curious, and enthusiastic students looking to apply classroom learning in an exciting, challenging, professional setting. The Program Operations Intern will support the day-to-day operations of the Information Services Internship & Residency Program while gaining hands-on experience in program administration, workflow optimization, recruitment operations, performance tracking, and process improvement. This role is ideal for a student interested in operations, analytics, workforce development, project coordination, and healthcare administration. The intern will gain exposure to how the IS internship program is managed while learning how operational processes align with department and organizational goals. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-focused, and interested in leveraging technology and automation tools to improve business processes. This position offers exposure to Power BI, Power Automate, reporting dashboards, recruitment operations, compliance tracking, program evaluation, and workflow automation initiatives. Key Responsibilities Support the day-to-day operations of the Internship & Residency Program, including onboarding, offboarding, compliance tracking, evaluations, documentation, and program communications. Monitor program performance through dashboards, reports, and tracking systems; identify trends, maintain data accuracy, and provide insights to support decision-making. Assist with recruitment activities, including candidate screening, applicant tracking, recruitment events, and talent pipeline management. Support intern evaluations by tracking timelines, coordinating meetings, managing documentation, and monitoring completion of required deliverables. Identify opportunities to improve workflows, increase efficiency, and enhance the intern experience through process optimization and data-driven recommendations. Assist with the design and implementation of workflow automations using Power Automate and other Microsoft technologies to reduce manual effort and streamline operations. Support internship events, on-site days, networking activities, and special projects that advance program goals and organizational initiatives. Preferred Qualifications Required Skills Strong organizational and time-management abilities. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Strong customer service and interpersonal skills. Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously. Detail-oriented with strong follow-through. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Word). Preferred Technical Skills Power BI Power Automate Excel reporting and data analysis SharePoint Microsoft Forms Basic workflow automation concepts General Program Requirements Student Workers are limited to 20 hours/week (40 hours/week while classes are not in session) and must not have any other jobs. Work a minimum of 12 hours/week (20 hours/week while classes are not in session) Must graduate May 2027 or later New hires must complete the following: TB test Drug screening Background check

jobs.title: Construction Project Manager Intern/Co-op (Summer 2027) at ARCO
jobs.description: Employer: ARCO - ARCO Design/Build Expires: 05/01/2027 ABOUT YOUAre you a passionate problem-solver who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment? Do you take pride in doing the right thing and delivering quality work with integrity? Are you excited to learn how construction projects come to life — from the first idea to the final walkthrough? If you answered “Yes!” — this opportunity was built for you. At ARCO Design/Build, we’re not just building structures — we’re building the next generation of industry leaders. Join us and discover what it means to be part of one of the nation’s top design/build construction firms. WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOUFour core values that guide our culture:Treat people fairly and do the right thingUnderstand our customers’ business and solve their problemsBe positive, upbeat, and have funCreate opportunities for individual financial success based on merit Here’s what you’ll get as part of our internship/co-op program:Competitive hourly pay with overtime opportunitiesHousing stipend available based on needMedical, dental, and vision insurance for interns working at least 3 monthsProfessional development through training and mentorshipCompany-sponsored lunches, happy hours, and networking eventsFully stocked kitchens with drinks and snacksA fun, inclusive work environment We don’t just invest in projects — we invest in people. From your first day, you’ll be part of a team that values growth, connection, and doing great work.ARCO is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all team members, interns, and co-ops. A DAY IN THE LIFEAs a Construction Design/Build Project Manager (DBM) Intern/Co-op, every day brings a new lesson. You’ll gain exposure to the full lifecycle of a project while working alongside experienced professionals who are invested in your growth.Here’s what you can expect:Concept to Completion Approach – Gain how ARCO manages projects from the initial concept through final delivery.Estimating and Takeoffs – Learn to describe project proposals and assign accurate dollar values.Scheduling – Assist in creating timelines for subcontractors/trades activities.Design Meetings – Attend meetings with the owner and design team, including structural engineers and architects.Reporting – Prepare weekly reports, document progress, and track meeting action items.Shadowing – Join project calls and site meetings to observe how our Design/Build Managers lead.Buyout – Send bid instructions, schedules, and drawings to subcontractors. Evaluate proposals and assist with awarding subcontracts.Permitting – Complete and submit permit applications with necessary documents and fees to city/county/fire authorities.Shop Drawing & Submittal Review – Receive and route submittals to DBMs and communicate approvals to subcontractors.Billing – Learn about subcontracts, change orders, pay requests, and pay applications.Job Site Visits – Visit job sites with DBMs to monitor project progress.Training & Learning – Attend offsite trainings and biweekly learning sessions provided by the Learning and Development team.Business Development – Gain exposure to how we build client relationships and implement industry-wide business development strategies.No matter where you’re starting from, you’ll leave this experience with valuable industry knowledge and a strong foundation for a future in construction. NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONSEnrolled in an accredited Civil, Mechanical, Architectural, Construction Management, Building Science, or Construction Engineering undergraduate or graduate program (other related engineering majors will be considered) Driver’s License Excellent verbal communication skills, attention to detail, and a strong work ethic Previous Co-op or Intern experience in construction preferred, but not required GPA 3.0 or higher preferred, but not required MAKE YOUR MOVEWith 38 offices nationwide, ARCO Design/Build is one of the fastest-growing construction firms in the country — and we’re just getting started. Ranked #3 on ENR’s Top 100 Design-Build Firms, we specialize in delivering high-quality industrial and commercial projects through a fully integrated approach. We’re proud to be 100% associate-owned, offering every full-time team member a stake in our success through our Employee Stock Ownership Program (ESOP). Whether you're looking to gain experience, find mentorship, or launch your career, you’ll find more than just an internship here — you’ll find opportunity, impact, and a team that values your growth. From day one, the opportunity for success at ARCO is limitless. ARCO does not accept unsolicited resumes from individual recruiters or third-party recruiting agencies without pre-approval from our Human Resources team. ARCO will not be responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes or candidates sent directly to our hiring managers. #LI-CM5 #LI-Onsite

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Product Manager Intern at Appian Corporation
jobs.description: Employer: Appian Corporation Expires: 05/16/2027 Our Product Management team at Appian is passionate about technology - we love making it, and we love using it. We operate at the intersection of engineering precision, user-centric design, and business strategy within an Agile-led environment that values collaboration and personal growth. By joining our structured university cohort, you will work within a small team of engineers to build simple, powerful features that expand our AI-Powered Process Automation platform.As a Product Manager Intern, you will transition your technical background into real-world software delivery. Moving beyond purely theoretical coursework, you will step in as an embedded product manager, collaborating with key stakeholders, defining acceptance criteria, and ensuring absolute Enterprise-Grade Orchestration with every iteration.This internship is based at our headquarters in McLean, Virginia. Appian was built on a culture of in-person collaboration, which we believe is a key driver of our mission to be the best. Interns in this program are expected to be in the office 5 days a week to fully experience our culture, learn directly from peers and mentors, and contribute to projects in a collaborative environment. Being in the office provides more opportunities to connect, learn, and celebrate with the exceptional people across Appian.Applicants considered for Summer 2027 - Students Only What You’ll DoOwn the Agile Backlog: Act as the embedded product owner for a highly skilled engineering squad, taking charge of backlog prioritization, feature sizing, and iterative sprint planning.Drive Collaborative Discovery: Share innovative ideas, analyze technical specifications, and gather continuous feedback through design sessions, user experience (UX) reviews, and usability mockups.Define Product Roadmaps: Partner with senior product leaders to structure enterprise software roadmaps, balancing long-term strategic investments with rapid feature delivery.Practice Stakeholder Negotiation: Empathize with conflicting stakeholder demands and developer constraints, applying data-driven negotiation skills to make optimal feature compromises.Conduct Impact Analysis: Monitor post-launch usability metrics and track user success parameters to verify that new releases address true customer needs.Participate in Passion Frameworks: Showcase your creative problem-solving skills during our department-led Hackathons and drive unique prototypes using dedicated Engineering Indie Time.Basic QualificationsEducation: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or Computer Engineering with a strong academic record. Must be returning to school following the completion of the Summer 2027 internship to continue degree requirements.Program Availability: Ability to commit to a full-time (40 hours/week) schedule for the duration of the 10-week summer program.Proven fluency in AI and LLMs, encompassing both the strategic development of AI-powered platform capabilities and the hands-on application of AI tools to accelerate daily workflows. Preferred QualificationsPrior experience in a technical internship or a portfolio of significant personal/academic projects. At this time, Appian will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization for this position. Thank you for your interest in joining our team! Please note that we will officially begin reviewing applications and scheduling interviews starting August 2026. We appreciate your patience and look forward to connecting with you then.At Appian, we embrace AI as part of how we work and innovate. While candidates are encouraged to use AI for preparation and learning, we restrict AI usage for live interviews and assessments unless otherwise specified. In some cases, AI use may be part of the assessment, and expectations will be communicated in advance. This internship pays $50.00 per hour ($8,666 per month). Pay and benefits are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation, bonus, or benefit plans.
